title: Troy ALPR governance and audit implementation update
summary: Request #1905 advances Troy's policy and audit chronology using current city records and reporting while preserving the gap between announced controls, platform configuration, and actual user activity.

sources.title: City Officials Announce Updated Flock Safety ALPR Policy Enhancements
City Council says Troy police gave incomplete data from surveillance cameras
Measure to limit Troy emergency powers, subject of two public hearings

gaps: Native Organization Audit, Network Audit, sharing exports and chief-exception query records remain unrecovered.
The final enacted/codified status of Local Law No. 4 was not established by the sources reviewed in this pass.

data.question: What can current public records establish about Troy's announced ALPR controls, 60-day implementation review, audit commitments and emergency-powers legislation?
data.method: Reused existing Troy investigation targets and reconciled the City of Troy's May 19 policy release, current City Council Agenda Center, and recent Times Union reporting.
data.framework: Announced policy, enacted law, platform configuration, audit exports and actual user behavior are separate evidence classes.
data.scope: Troy ALPR governance, annual audit commitment, National Lookup exception policy, 60-day review and Local Law No. 4 hearing chronology.
findings: The City of Troy announced a 60-day working period on May 19, 2026 and stated that annual ALPR audits would be provided to the mayor and City Council.

The same city release stated that National Lookup would remain disabled except for violent-felony cases with individualized Police Chief authorization and prohibited immigration-enforcement use and monitoring of First Amendment activity.

The current City Council Agenda Center lists Local Law No. 4 public hearings on July 23 and a third hearing on August 6, establishing that the required hearing process advanced beyond the earlier proposal stage.

Times Union reported that during the 60-day review police supplied full information for only 30 of 81 cases identified by Councilmember Noreen McKee as relevant, while the police report included 826 searches; city officials disputed whether the request had been fully satisfied.

As of the reviewed records, the public evidence does not establish that announced safeguards were mirrored exactly in Flock configuration or user activity, and the final enacted/codified status of Local Law No. 4 remains unresolved.
conclusions: Troy's governance record now supports a documented policy-and-review chronology, but native audit/configuration evidence is still required before treating the announced controls as implemented controls.
The 60-day review produced a concrete data-quality dispute that should be preserved rather than smoothed into a single city position.
recommendations: Recover native Organization Audit, Network Audit, SharedNetworks and configuration exports for the 60-day period.
Recover every Police Chief National Lookup exception and resulting query identifier.
Recover the August 6 regular-meeting record and any later mayoral action, veto, override or codification for Local Law No. 4.
counterarguments: The mayor and police leadership disputed the council characterization that the requested 60-day information was incomplete.
A hearing listing proves process activity, not enactment.
limitations: No native Flock export was available in this pass.
No final codified Local Law No. 4 text was authenticated in the reviewed sources.
unresolved: Did Local Law No. 4 pass after the August 6 hearing, and was it vetoed or overridden?
Were the announced National Lookup and sharing restrictions actually reflected in platform configuration?
What did the first annual audit contain and when was it delivered?
